When it's 5 degrees out, heat is about more than comfort: a cold house can mean frozen pipes by morning. Call any hour. We repair all makes and models of heating equipment.

**Water heaters.** A water heater usually fails at the tank. You find out when the water goes lukewarm, or when there's water on the floor around it.

Sediment builds up in the bottom of the tank over the years and the tank wears out. Servicing it before then is cheaper than replacing it in a hurry. We replace and install new water heaters and give you a free estimate.
We also service existing ones to keep them running.

sections.heading: What Usually Goes Wrong
body: Most AC failures come down to a short list.
list: **Capacitor.** A small part that gives the motors their starting push. The unit hums, the fan doesn't spin and nothing cools.
**Blower motor.** The fan inside that moves cool air through the house. When it fails, the outdoor unit may run but little air reaches the rooms.
**Refrigerant leak.** Low refrigerant means weak cooling and, eventually, ice on the lines or the indoor coil.
**Frozen coil.** Ice builds when airflow is restricted or refrigerant is low. A clogged filter is a common cause.
**Thermostat.** Sometimes the system is fine and the control that talks to it isn't.
**Condenser.** The outdoor unit takes the most abuse, from heat, dirt and Kansas weather.
tail: Many of these are a single part, not a new air conditioner.
The symptoms overlap, which is why guessing costs money. Warm air can mean a weak capacitor, a dead blower or a low charge, and each one is a different repair.

sections.heading: What to Check Before You Call
body: A few checks cost nothing and sometimes solve the problem.
list: **Check the thermostat.** Make sure it's set to cool and set below the room temperature.
**Check the filter.** A clogged filter chokes airflow, and that can freeze the coil.
**Check the breaker.** A tripped breaker can shut off the outdoor unit.
**Look at the outdoor unit.** Clear leaves and debris from around it.
tail: If the AC is still warm after that, turn it off and call. A system that keeps running hot, frozen or short of refrigerant strains the compressor, the most expensive part in it. A repair that's a capacitor today can be a compressor next week.

sections.heading: What Usually Goes Wrong
body: Furnace problems come down to a short list.
list: **Igniter or flame sensor.** The furnace tries to start, clicks or clicks off and never stays lit. Both parts wear out, and a dirty sensor can shut the burners off early.
**Blower motor.** The fan that pushes warm air through the ducts. If it fails, the furnace may run but little heat reaches the rooms.
**Control board.** The circuit board that runs the startup sequence. When it fails, the furnace may not respond at all.
**Dirty filter.** A clogged filter restricts airflow, makes the furnace overheat and shut down, and then it restarts and cycles.
**Thermostat.** Sometimes the furnace is fine and the control isn't.
**Heat exchanger.** The metal that heats the air without mixing it with exhaust. Cracks and rust here are a safety problem, and they're why an inspection is worth it.
tail: Most of these are single parts, not a new furnace, even on an older unit.

sections.heading: We Find the Cause Before We Replace Anything
body: Replacing parts until the problem goes away costs you money. We find the cause first, then fix it.

A furnace that cycles on and off may be overheating behind a clogged filter or a closed-off return. Or a dirty flame sensor can't confirm the flame, so the furnace shuts the burners off a few seconds after they light.
Each one looks the same from the hallway: the heat starts, then stops. That's why the diagnosis comes first.
You hear what we found and what the repair involves.
